text: The year was 1889, and the last great oak forest in the region was a spectacle that many traveled miles to behold. Arthur, a young naturalist, stood in awe among the ancient trees, a leather-bound journal in hand as he recorded notes about species that had become legends. This sacred grove, unbeknownst to him, was about to become the centerpiece of a historic preservation effort that would challenge the industrial metropolis encroaching upon the natural world. The city, located in France, known for the Eiffel Tower, was rapidly expanding its iron and steam infrastructure, threatening to consume the remaining wild spaces.
